prompt: Three vertices of a rectangle are $(-1, 2)$, $(5, 2)$, and $(5, 6)$. What is the fourth vertex?
hint: The sides of this rectangle are horizontal and vertical. That means its corners use only two different $x$-values and two different $y$-values.

hints.title: 🪜 Try a simpler one
hints.text: Try a rectangle with corners $(0, 0)$, $(3, 0)$ and $(3, 2)$ first. Its fourth corner is $(0, 2)$, which takes its $x$ from one corner and its $y$ from another.
The sides of this rectangle are horizontal and vertical. That means its corners use only two different $x$-values and two different $y$-values.
The $x$-values so far are $-1, 5, 5$ and the $y$-values are $2, 2, 6$. Each value must be used exactly twice, so find the $x$ and the $y$ that have only been used once.
$x = -1$ and $y = 6$ have each been used once, so the fourth vertex is $(-1, 6)$.

explanation: $(-1, 2)$ and $(5, 2)$ share $y = 2$, so they form the bottom side of the rectangle.
$(5, 2)$ and $(5, 6)$ share $x = 5$, so they form the right side.
The missing corner is on the left side, so $x = -1$, and on the top side, so $y = 6$.
So the fourth vertex of the rectangle is $(-1, 6)$.

alternativeExplanations.title: Match opposite sides
steps: Top edge at $y = 6$ must also run from $-1$ to $5$.
